task.goal: Make the parser at least 2x faster on the representative corpus.
task.context: The parser is single-threaded TypeScript. Profiling shows time in token construction and recursive descent. Inputs are mostly ASCII source files between 2 KB and 500 KB.

constraints.text: Do not change the public parser API or AST shape.
The package must remain pure JavaScript and run on every currently supported Node.js platform.
Peak memory should not grow by more than 15 percent.

success.text: Median throughput is at least 2.0x the recorded baseline on the representative corpus.
All existing tests and differential parser checks pass.

candidates.title: Remove hot-path token allocations
candidates.summary: Represent transient tokens as offsets into the source buffer.
candidates.mechanism: Keep start and end offsets during recursive descent and materialize token objects only when they become part of the public AST.
assumptions: Token construction and garbage collection are meaningful measured costs.
risks: Lazy materialization could expose incorrect source spans.
validation: Run the complete and differential test suites.
Compare allocation counts, peak memory, and corpus throughput against baseline.

candidates.title: Pool temporary token objects
candidates.summary: Reuse token objects instead of allocating them for every parse.
candidates.mechanism: Introduce a bounded per-parse token pool and reset objects as the parser advances.
assumptions: Temporary token allocation is the dominant source of garbage collection.
risks: A reused token could escape and be mutated after publication.
validation: Compare allocations and throughput against baseline.

candidates.title: Memoize repeated grammar decisions
candidates.summary: Cache expensive lookahead decisions at stable source offsets.
candidates.mechanism: Store the result of selected ambiguous grammar predicates in a bounded offset-indexed cache for the duration of one parse.
assumptions: The same ambiguous predicates are evaluated repeatedly at identical offsets.
risks: Cache bookkeeping may cost more than the repeated predicates.
Unbounded entries could violate the memory target.
validation: Instrument cache hit rate and size.
Benchmark with and without the cache on each corpus category.

candidates.title: Add an ASCII byte fast path
candidates.summary: Parse common ASCII identifiers and punctuation without building intermediate strings.
candidates.mechanism: Recognize the dominant ASCII token classes directly from code units, falling back to the existing lexer for Unicode and uncommon syntax.
assumptions: ASCII-heavy files dominate the representative corpus.
Lexer overhead is a measured hotspot.
risks: Fast and fallback paths could disagree at Unicode boundaries.
validation: Differentially compare both paths over generated ASCII and Unicode inputs.
Benchmark each corpus category and measure fallback frequency.

candidates.title: Add cross-call incremental parsing
candidates.summary: Reuse unchanged subtrees between repeated parser calls.
candidates.mechanism: Persist a source-range keyed tree cache across invocations and invalidate ranges affected by edits.
assumptions: Most real parser calls are edits of a previously parsed document.
risks: The current API provides neither document identity nor edit ranges.
Cache invalidation could change observable AST identity.
validation: Create an edit-trace benchmark and compare full reparsing with cached reparsing.

candidates.title: Parse grammar regions in parallel
candidates.summary: Split an input into regions and parse them on worker threads.
candidates.mechanism: Pre-scan for top-level boundaries, send regions to worker threads, and merge the resulting AST fragments.
assumptions: Top-level regions can be found cheaply before parsing.
Worker startup and serialization are small relative to parse time.
risks: Grammar state crosses proposed region boundaries.
Small and medium inputs may become slower.
validation: Run correctness tests on boundary-heavy syntax.
Benchmark by input size with worker overhead separated.

candidates.title: Rewrite the lexer as a native extension
candidates.summary: Move lexing into a Rust Node.js addon.
candidates.mechanism: Implement lexing in Rust, expose tokens through N-API, and keep recursive descent in TypeScript.
assumptions: Native lexing is fast enough to offset the JavaScript/native boundary.
risks: Introduces platform-specific builds and distribution artifacts.
Boundary conversion may erase the expected gain.
validation: Run compatibility tests on every target platform.
Benchmark lexing and end-to-end parsing separately.
